threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'trolley' instead of a 'shopping trolley' and look confused when locals say 'bag for life'.
Caught a late 133 last night, overheard a group debating the merits of jellied eels. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I remember the day I spotted a group of kids using an old tire as a makeshift basketball hoop in a random park. That's when it hit me—this place has character.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find a hidden bar in a laundromat where DJs spin vinyl while you wait for your spin cycle.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you’re a local when you can spot the tourists trying to figure out how to cross 24th without getting run over by a bus.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy serenading Muni riders with a ukulele during the morning rush. Only in San Francisco would folks break into spontaneous applause between stops.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Park Güell but miss the hidden murals on the back streets of Gràcia. The real soul of the barrio is in the small plazas and local cafés.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their wide-eyed wonder at the simplest street performers, while locals just walk past without a glance.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot a newbie when they queue for an hour at the market, oblivious to the pop-up stalls just around the corner with fresher produce.
Caught a night bus by the market, and the guy next to me was arguing with his phone. Thought he lost the plot until I saw the live train updates on his screen.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The random karaoke night at the back of a kebab shop on Sonnenallee, when everyone joined in, even the grumpy old man at the counter.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a 24-hour Kebab stand that doubles as an art gallery. Midnight snack and culture, all in one bite.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a real local by how they grip the BART handrail—less iron grip, more casual lean. Tourists cling on like their life depends on it.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: On the 31 Balboa yesterday, a guy serenaded us with a guitar while a pigeon critiqued his singing from the floor. Classic San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the parks are just for lounging, but locals use them for community events, secret music gigs, and spontaneous petanque games.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their confusion over which side to walk on the narrow sidewalks—locals move in a straight line like they’re part of traffic.
